BASED NUT · UNITED STATES

SHOW ME
THE NUTS.

Nut harvests, wild mast and growers across the United States and its territories.

USA + U.S. territories.
50 states · Puerto Rico · U.S. Virgin Islands · Guam · Northern Mariana Islands · American Samoa
$14.84B2025 farm-gate value mapped
212025 state harvest records
5U.S. territories mapped
5local grower locations

The nut map

Turn layers on from the map. Harvests, growers, territories and USDA Forest Service wild-mast density.

2025 · USDA NASS
MAP LAYERS
LOADING USDA FIA DENSITY…
LOWER30 m modeled aboveground biomass · tons/acreHIGHER

2025 harvest ledger

Production and farm-gate value reported by USDA NASS. Dollar values are already reported by USDA where available; no retail-price multiplier is used.

NutStateHarvestPriceFarm-gate valueSource

Territories

Coconut is the strongest recurring nut-like crop in the current territorial Census of Agriculture data.

* Puerto Rico reports a combined “fruits and coconuts” sales value. Guam, CNMI and USVI do not publish a coconut-only dollar value in these tables; the page shows the associated fruit/nut specialty-farm sales figure instead. American Samoa reports coconut sales directly.

Growers on the ground

Public farm, orchard and processing locations tied to the same producing regions shown above.

Wild mast density

Where nut- and fruit-bearing forest trees concentrate across the Lower 48.

2025 · VIRGINIA

Acorns on the trees

White oak 22 · Red oak 21.3

Average percent of surveyed tree crowns carrying acorns. 32 hard-mast sites statewide.

Virginia DWR ↗
2025 · WEST VIRGINIA

18 mast species surveyed

+2% vs long-term · +16% vs 2024

Hard mast increased statewide; beech, hickory and walnut were above both 2024 and the long-term average.
